presets.importExportIntro: Save the current settings to a JSON file (e.g. for sharing with a teammate or version control), or load a previously-exported settings file. Importing replaces the current form with the file's contents — press Save at the bottom to persist.

webhook.intro1: Webhook fired once when each crawl finishes. Single
webhook.intro2: with a JSON summary (start URL, duration, total URLs, status mix, every non-zero issue count). Empty disables.
webhook.outro: Compatible with Slack incoming webhooks (the JSON shape is rich enough for Slack to render plain text), Zapier "Catch Hook" triggers, Discord webhooks, and custom HTTP endpoints.

auth.intro: HTTP authentication applied on every request. Useful for staging environments behind Basic auth, or APIs that require a Bearer token. Digest is not supported (challenge-response state machine).

network.intro: Network-level controls: proxy override, file-extension exclusion, redirect hop cap.
network.savedProfilesDesc: Save multiple `(name, URL)` pairs and switch between them via the dropdown below. The active profile overrides the Proxy URL field and the HTTPS_PROXY env var. Empty selection falls back to the Proxy URL above.
network.noSavedProfiles: No saved profiles — add one below.

duplicates.intro: Near-duplicate detection. After every crawl, body text is hashed with a 64-bit SimHash, and pages whose hashes lie within the configured Hamming distance of each other are clustered as near-duplicates. Surfaced under
duplicates.maxHamming: Max Hamming distance (0 = exact only, 12 = very loose, 0 disables)
duplicates.thresholdHint: Lower = stricter. 3 is the SF-equivalent default. Pages with too little body content (<50 characters) are excluded from clustering regardless of threshold.
duplicates.costBody: SimHash adds ~5-10 ms per page during crawl; clustering itself runs after the last URL completes (~3-10 s at 1M URLs, <500 ms at 100K).

hardware.intro: Resource caps for the crawler process. Useful for keeping the machine usable while crawling large sites (1M+ URLs).
hardware.memoryHint: When the crawler's RSS exceeds this, the queue auto-pauses and resumes once memory drops below 80% of the cap. Soft cap — does not enforce a hard heap limit.
hardware.queueHint: Hard cap on pending URLs held in memory. Excess discoveries are dropped silently — bounds peak heap during fan-out bursts (large sitemaps, dense link graphs). Set conservatively if memory is tight.
hardware.priorityHint1: OS scheduler hint. Lowering priority lets the rest of the machine stay responsive during heavy crawls. Effective on next crawl start; may require elevated privileges on some platforms. For raw CPU concurrency, see

content.intro: How crawled HTML is stored on disk. Disable body snapshots to keep the project file small when you don't need the View Source detail tab; tighten the cap for sites with adversarially-large pages.
content.storeBody: Store raw HTML body per page

crawlAnalysis.intro: Per-pass post-crawl analysis toggles. Each pass runs after the HTTP fetch phase finishes and feeds different issue filters. Skip passes you don't need to shave wall-clock on large crawls; the related issue counters quietly read as 0 until the pass runs.

issues.v2Body: Today every issue check runs unconditionally and surfaces in the sidebar. The plan is to let you silence specific checks per-project (e.g. disable "Description = Title" on a CMS that's known to do it intentionally). Until that ships, hide rows you don't care about by collapsing the sidebar group, or filter them out via the Advanced filter on each tab.

advanced.intro: Lower-level caps and link-follow toggles. Defaults are tuned for typical SEO audits — only touch these if you know why.

cookies.intro: Cookie policy applied to every fetch. The crawler is otherwise stateless across requests; this setting controls whether Set-Cookie response headers are recorded for the cookie-flag issue checks (Missing Secure / HttpOnly / SameSite).
cookies.valuesNeverStored2: stored in the project file regardless of this setting — only the security flag (Secure / HttpOnly / SameSite) counts are kept.

rendering.intro: JavaScript rendering uses headless Chromium (Playwright) to fetch the post-load DOM after scripts execute. Required for SPA / hydration-only content. Significantly slower than text mode — every URL pays a browser-launch and wait cost. Enable in the Crawler panel under Rendering Mode.
rendering.disabledHint: Rendering Mode is currently set to Text or Old AJAX. Switch to JavaScript Rendering in the Crawler panel to apply the settings below.
rendering.resourceBlockingHint: Block resource types before they hit the network — speeds up rendering at the cost of fidelity. Images and fonts are typically safe to block for SEO crawls; blocking scripts defeats the point of JS rendering.
rendering.screenshotHint: PNG screenshots written to a sidecar folder next to the .seoproject file. Adds ~150–500ms per URL — leave off unless you need them for the visual audit.

perHostUa.intro: Override the User-Agent on a per-host basis. Useful when crawling a mobile subdomain with the mobile-Googlebot UA in the same run as the desktop site, or when a CDN serves a different page based on the requester's UA. The first matching pattern wins; the global User-Agent (Requests tab) is the fallback.

perHostUa.empty: No per-host overrides yet — add one below.

storage.intro: Default folder for new .seoproject files. Save As dialogs open here by default; the Open dialog is not constrained.
storage.resetTitle: Reset to the OS Documents folder
storage.note: Active crawl data lives in the app's user-data directory until you Save As — the path above only controls where Save As starts. Changing this won't move any existing project files.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: FreeCrawl is local-first — crawl results, project files, and URLs you visit never leave your machine.
privacy.telemetryHelp: Off by default. When on, aggregated counts of feature use (e.g. "export ran", "report opened") may be sent — never URLs, project contents, or crawl results.
privacy.statusNote: No telemetry endpoint is currently wired up. Toggling this preference is recorded but nothing is transmitted in the current build. The toggle is exposed now so consent state persists across upgrades when a future build adds an endpoint.
